chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Abdillah ibn al-Qasim, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Beware of speech when the two circumcised parts meet, for it causes deafness/muteness.'

key_terms.الْخِتَانَيْنِ: The two circumcised parts (penis and vagina)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on speaking during intercourse in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises minimizing speech during sexual intercourse, linking excessive talk to 'khuras' (often interpreted as temporary muteness or loss of voice). This reflects the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and spiritual mindfulness (*hudhur al-qalb*) during intimacy, viewing the act as a form of worship when performed with presence and restraint.
